The result favors fishing, diving and simple couple cruising over accommodation privacy.

ModelVariations.Description: The Sport Cruiser redesign uses the same basic 27 family concept but replaces the aft cabin with a large open cockpit and simpler forward accommodation.

ModelCharacter: The utility-oriented redesign of the Albin 27: same compact semi-displacement platform, but with a huge open cockpit, semi-enclosed helm and simplified cabin for fishing, diving and day-oriented cruising.
DesignLineage: The 27 Sport Cruiser was introduced in 1985 as a redesigned version of the 27 Family Cruiser.
It retains the 26'9" LOA, 9'8" beam, shallow draft and full-length keel of the Family Cruiser.
The aft sleeping cabin was sacrificed in favor of a much larger working cockpit and better engine access.
It remained in production alongside the Family Cruiser through 1995.
OwnershipCharacter: One of the simpler Albins to own: single diesel, excellent engine access and minimal interior systems. Buyers give up the Family Cruiser's separate aft cabin in exchange for far better cockpit utility.

ModelVariations.Name: Custom and semi-custom finish variation
ModelVariations.Description: Duffy hulls have been finished in different commercial and recreational configurations; machinery, house, flybridge, tankage and interior layout are hull-specific.

ModelCharacter: The modernized larger sibling of the Duffy 35: a Spencer Lincoln 37-foot built-down lobsterboat with additional beam, headroom and carrying capacity plus underbody changes intended to improve speed and fuel efficiency. It has become especially popular as a custom couple's Downeast cruiser.
DesignLineage: The first Duffy 37 hull came out in October 1999.
Atlantic Boat describes the 37 as a slightly larger evolution of the Duffy 35 with underbody changes for greater speed and efficiency.
The hull was offered in both workboat and cruiser configurations with different main-bulkhead locations.
The 37 remains a current Duffy kit size and has been finished by multiple specialist yards, so accommodations vary materially.
OwnershipCharacter: Excellent combination of single-diesel efficiency, protected running gear and enough volume for true cruising accommodations. Semi-custom finishes mean one 37 may be a simple workboat and another a generator/air-conditioning/thruster-equipped yacht; maintenance burden follows the finish, not merely the hull.

ModelVariations.Name: Prairie 36 / Atlantic 37 lineage
ModelVariations.Description: After Prairie closed, Atlantic Yachts acquired the Prairie 36 molds and reintroduced the design as the Atlantic 37 Double Cabin.

ModelCharacter: The larger Jack Hargrave development of the Prairie 29 concept: a beamy American-built double-cabin semi-displacement trawler with full keel, twin diesels, two private heads with separate showers and unusually generous liveaboard accommodations for 36 feet.
DesignLineage: Prairie introduced the 36 Coastal Cruiser in 1979 after the strong reception of the Prairie 29.
The 36 retained the 29's soft-chine semi-displacement/full-keel design language while adding a true two-stateroom, two-head interior.
Prairie produced the 36 until early 1982, when the company closed.
Atlantic Yachts acquired the tooling and reintroduced the same hull in 1982 as the Atlantic 37 Double Cabin, creating a direct Prairie 36 → Atlantic 37 lineage.
OwnershipCharacter: A comfortable Great Loop/coastal liveaboard platform with protected running gear, shallow draft and excellent machinery access. Twin engines, two heads, large tankage and 22,000 pounds of boat increase upkeep, but systems remain conventional and the direct Atlantic 37 continuation helps preserve owner knowledge and parts solutions.
